research_rationale: The complete original creates Treasury and FRBNY transfer machinery for funds connected to UNSCR 778, with financial-institution directions conditioned on Treasury determinations. Its repayment contingencies and section 4 discharges are not a calendar sunset or proof of exhaustion. No earlier ending actor is indicated in the complete bounded search; EO:13350 expressly revokes EO:12817 and section 10 establishes July 30, 2004 at 12:01 a.m. EDT. Section 4 is expressly analyzed separately: discharge and good-faith immunity for transfers/conduct already undertaken, and pre-transfer claims, are accrued consequences preserved by EO:13350 section 1. Neither those savings nor the definitions and no-private-right language independently retain fresh transfer or holding authority after revocation. The inventory restores the missed section 2 and eliminates a heading-only section 8. Full-freeze audit: The frozen onefile has the same complete original and complete EO:13350 context, with no newly indicated earlier ending. Treasury determinations, UN repayment and FRBNY holding/investment contingencies specify administration rather than an automatic sunset. Section 4 is separately re-read: full acquittance/discharge arises to the extent of compliant transfers, good-faith immunity attaches to historical conduct, and pre-transfer rights/debts/claims are preserved. EO:13350 section 1 expressly saves prior actions and matured rights/duties, leaving those accrued residuals intact. They do not authorize fresh transfers or establish an independent forward command after express revocation. July 30, 2004 at 12:01 a.m. EDT remains the first demonstrated complete end, not the July 29 signing date.
